- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling below 70), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–4% for next 2–3 periods.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and model still forecasts high prices, apply downward bias correction of 3–6% to avoid overconfidence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days); apply 1–3% downward adjustment to first 5 forecasts.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.68, -0.38, +1.00), model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average to smooth forecast.
